text:
Omar Malik: Heads up — we saw a perf regression on the TP+PP 8-GPU job after the kernel-selector change last night. 15% higher p99 latency for short-chat workload (seq<=512). Anyone else seeing the same?
Lee Chen: yup repro'd on two-node EFA runs. trace looks like bigger gaps during KV sync / all-reduce windows.
Chris Patel: can you paste the traces? nsys / ncu output helps.
Lee Chen: here's the quick nsys timeline snippet (condensed):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o run1
Timeline: kernel launches spike, then large idle on device, then AllReduce op spikes ~3.2ms each (used to be ~1.1ms)
Host->device memcpy small but frequent around KV sync timestamps
```
Omar Malik: interesting — the kernel-selector change picked different GEMM kernels for some layers (more small-matrix launches). maybe kernel launch overhead + less comm/compute overlap.
Sia Rivera: I think two things are colliding: 1) selector favors tensor-core fused kernels that change launch shape (more kernels), 2) our KV cache synchronization still does global all-reduce every step for checkpointed KV shards. Combined they increase small-kernel count and amplify all-reduce scheduling stalls.
Chris Patel: infra metrics show EFA tx saturated during peaks. infra-bot: EFA link 100Gbps per link, avg util ~88% at peak windows, PCIe-bound copies show bursts.
infra-bot: (automated) node-ids: i-0a1b2c / i-0d3e4f, nvlink pairs healthy, no ECC.
Lee Chen: I ran `nvprof` + `nvtx` and saw that many small GEMM kernels are non-fused fallback variants. AllReduce latency per-step jumped ~2.5x when fallback kernels used.
Omar Malik: actionable question — are we able to route KV syncs to prefer NVLink-local peers before crossing EFA? topology-aware sync could reduce cross-node all-reduce volume.
Sia Rivera: yes we can add a routing heuristic in the KV sync planner: greedily reduce KV shards via intra-rack NVLink rings first, then inter-rack EFA. Pseudocode:
```
if (topology.has_local_nvlink_ring()) {
  schedule.reduce(local_ring_shards);
}
schedule.reduce(inter_node_shards, stitch_via_efa);
```
Chris Patel: also think kernel selector should surface a cost estimate: extra kernel launches vs fused throughput. We could prefer the older fused-kernel for seq<=512 and tp_size>1 until we validate overlap improvements.
Lee Chen: quick experiment: forced selector -> fused_kern for short seq: p99 drops back ~10%, AllReduce median down ~1.2ms. still slightly above baseline but much better.
Omar Malik: nice. so two parallel fixes: (A) topology-aware KV reduce ordering, (B) conservative selector for small-seq workloads.
Sia Rivera: I'll draft a small selector heuristic change and a config flag `REDWOOD_SELECTOR_HEURISTIC=conservative_shortseq` so we can canary. patch snippet: 
```
- if (seq_len <= 1024) choose_best_by_flops();
+ if (seq_len <= 512 && tp_size > 1) choose_fused_kern_v1();
+ else choose_best_by_flops();
```
Chris Patel: I'll add an instrumentation point to stamp KV-sync NVTX events so we can correlate exact network op timings in the next profile.
infra-bot: scheduled canary deployment tomorrow 09:00 PT to group alpha hosts.
Omar Malik: plan for tomorrow: Lee runs single-node nvlink-only ncu to confirm purely local behavior, Chris adds NVTX KV stamps, Sia lands heuristic behind flag, I'll monitor canary.
Lee Chen: running nvlink-only now, will post results in thread.
Sia Rivera: PR opened WIP, will ping here when ready for review.
Chris Patel: if canary looks good, we'll roll to production staggered with traffic shaping to avoid EFA saturation. :thumbsup:
Omar Malik: thanks team — let's try to keep KV sync event frequency as low as possible until we confirm heuristics.
Lee Chen: quick note — also seeing a small increase in host-side memcpy scheduling latency when kernel count is high; might need to coalesce small memcpy calls in the runtime. filing perf follow-up.
Chris Patel: filing infra ticket to track EFA saturation mitigation (queueing / traffic shaping).
Sia Rivera: noted. I'll include a microbenchmark in the PR to show p99 before/after for seq=128/256/512.
Omar Malik: OK wrapping up. updates tomorrow after canary. :white_check_mark:
